correctness.rationale: For cubic graph P_j=(x+jh,(x+jh)^3), the two successive second differences are 6h^2(x+h) and 6h^2(x+2h). Their simultaneous vanishing is exactly N|6h^2x and N|6h^3 and ensures every further second difference vanishes. At p^k with e=v_p(6), step valuation s must satisfy 3s+e>=k and each step has p^min(k,2s+e) valid x. Summing step valuations gives the formula, with p=2,3 obtained from p^2 lifting. Local minimum step valuations give maximal additive order; CRT attains it with x=0. Exhaustive finite tests corroborate.

value.rationale: The two natural invariants are fully classified: the sharp maximal length of distinct affine progressions and the exact all-moduli count of four-term configurations. A prime-field cubic graph generally has no genuine four-term AP, while nilpotent prime-power lifting creates arbitrarily long progressions with sharp exponent and special behavior at 2 and 3. The complete valuation strata and CRT product formula are useful local information beyond a yes/no existence check, without requiring a downstream general theorem.
